def test_set_columns_with_dataframe():
    # Case: setting a DataFrame as new columns copies that data
    # (with delayed copy with CoW)
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]})
    df2 = pd.DataFrame({"c": [7, 8, 9], "d": [10, 11, 12]})

    df[["c", "d"]] = df2

    assert np.shares_memory(get_array(df, "c"), get_array(df2, "c"))
    # and modifying the set DataFrame does not modify the original DataFrame
    df2.iloc[0, 0] = 0
    tm.assert_series_equal(df["c"], pd.Series([7, 8, 9], name="c"))

def test_rename_columns_modify_parent():
    # Case: renaming columns returns a new dataframe
    # + afterwards modifying the original (parent) dataframe
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6], "c": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]})
    df2 = df.rename(columns=str.upper)
    df2_orig = df2.copy()

    assert np.shares_memory(get_array(df2, "A"), get_array(df, "a"))
    df.iloc[0, 0] = 0
    assert not np.shares_memory(get_array(df2, "A"), get_array(df, "a"))
    assert np.shares_memory(get_array(df2, "C"), get_array(df, "c"))

    # GH#65107 the zero-copy fast path for a sorted MultiIndex returns a view
    #  of the source for non-consolidated (multi-block) frames; ensure CoW
    #  still tracks the reference so mutating the result leaves the source

    df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], "y": ["p", "q", "r", "s"]}, index=idx)
    df_orig = df.copy()
    result = df.unstack()
